question: Decided on by the EU’s Member States on 8 February 2024, the EUNAVFOR ASPIDES military operation will deploy EU Member State warships to the Red Sea to protect cargo vessels, working in close cooperation with Operation Prosperity Guardian. The assignment is intended to be defensive in nature. 1.
Will the assignment involve sharing maritime situational awareness data with Operation Prosperity Guardian?
Could this data also be used for offensive operations?
answer: Council Decision (CFSP) 2024/583 of 8 February 2024 on a European Union maritime security operation to safeguard freedom of navigation in relation to the Red Sea crisis established Operation EUNAVFOR ASPIDES.

The mission of EUNAVFOR ASPIDES is to contribute to maritime security along the main sea lines of communication in the assigned Area of Operation, in cooperation with other major actors, including Operation Prosperity Guardian.

For this purpose, the High Representative is authorised to exchange with Operation Prosperity Guardian, through the respective Headquarters, classified information relevant to the purposes of EUNAVFOR ASPIDES up to ‘SECRET UE/EU SECRET’ level, in cases where an exchange at theatre level is necessary for operational reasons.
